memory_update.text: PI should be tracked as the highest-relevance underfollowed public-market candidate for the retail RFID and item-level inventory-accuracy node; verify retail adoption breadth beyond apparel and footwear.

RSKD opens a digital-shrink sub-lane: ecommerce fraud, chargebacks, returns abuse, refund claims, and policy-abuse analytics are adjacent to physical shrink but may have different unit economics and risk profiles.
NSSC is a speculative second-order store-security candidate; retail exposure exists in product/vertical language but materiality must be proven before it survives later Serenity layers.
The node splits into at least three investable sub-lanes: item-level RFID/inventory accuracy, digital fraud/returns-abuse software, and physical store hardening/access-control infrastructure.

Many pure-play retail loss-prevention assets are private or embedded inside larger companies, including Sensormatic inside Johnson Controls and Checkpoint Systems inside CCL Industries; public-market mapping therefore requires supplier and component-level screens.

summary: Expanded the universe around retail shrink, RFID inventory accuracy, ecommerce fraud, access control, and store-security infrastructure. The strongest underfollowed direct chokepoint candidate is Impinj, because its RAIN RFID platform is explicitly tied to retail item visibility and inventory accuracy. Riskified adds a digital-shrink lane through ecommerce fraud, chargebacks, policy abuse, returns, and refund claims. NAPCO is a more speculative second-order store-security and access-control supplier with retail mentioned but not yet proven as a material vertical. Zebra is included as a reference/context name because its RFID and data-capture products are directly relevant, although its market cap and visibility are above the preferred underfollowed range.
